item.title: All-optical thin-film lithium niobate memristor
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02048-1 Oxygen-ion implantation allows the direct fabrication of photonic memristors in thin-film lithium niobate. The resulting devices combine 3-bit non-volatile optical memory, submicrosecond responses and femtojoule-level switching energies.

item.description: arXiv:2611.13476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. item.title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
item.description: arXiv:2611.13570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. item.description: arXiv:2611.13589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dispersions and quality factors of a metallic nanoshell's plasmons may be readily tuned by varying the thickness of the nanoshell. This is because 1. Thickness determines the hybridization between the two nanoshell boundaries and 2. Thickness affects the electronic surface scattering rate and, therefore, the non-radiative decay rates of the plasmonic resonances. item.title: SGAA: Independent active alignment of optical subgroups with uncompensated aberrations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncompensated subgroup aberrations complicate subgroup-level active alignment (AA), as local image-quality extrema do not directly indicate the target alignment state. We propose SGAA, an image-learning-based method for independent active alignment of optical subgroups. item.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.14119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. item.description: arXiv:2611.14133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. item.description: arXiv:2611.14205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. item.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.14293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. item.description: arXiv:2611.13319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). item.description: arXiv:2611.13351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. item.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
item.description: arXiv:2611.13936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. item.title: CV-TF-QKD
item.description: arXiv:2611.14044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. item.description: arXiv:2611.14447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. item.title: Pure-blue quantum-dot light-emitting diodes with minimal efficiency roll-off and high brightness
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02041-8 Quantum dots with compositionally graded shells enhance quantum-dot LED performance, achieving pure-blue emission with a peak external quantum efficiency of 23.8%, 95% of which is retained at a luminance of 50,000 cd m−2.

item.title: Scientists discover new way to control magnetic waves for future quantum technologies
item.description: Researchers at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Ames National Laboratory have discovered a way to control the handedness of magnons, tiny magnetic waves that can carry information through materials. By changing the material's magnetic state with an external magnetic field, they were able to switch magnon behavior, a finding with potential applications in quantum information and quantum computing technologies. Their findings are published in Physical Review Letters.

item.title: Quantum could solve AI energy drain, says tech founder
item.description: Quantum computers could curb the vast energy demands of artificial intelligence data centers with their ability to run complex calculations, one of the tech's pioneers told AFP.

item.title: Optical control stabilizes cold-atom comagnetometry
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02043-6 The use of tailored laser fields improves the coherence times of two co-trapped ytterbium isotopes, resulting in the rejection of magnetic-field noise by more than thirty-thousand-fold, opening the way to improved comagnetometry.

item.title: Measuring hard X-ray attosecond pulses
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02037-4 The generation and characterization of high-power X-ray attosecond pulses is a challenging research frontier in free-electron laser science. Now, researchers at the Linac Coherent Light Source have demonstrated experimental confirmation and measurement of hard X-ray pulses reaching 100-attosecond durations.

item.title: Classical–quantum light interactions could make complex quantum behavior easier to simulate
item.description: An international collaboration demonstrates that classical nonlinear dynamics can drive single- and two-photon states to thermalize, opening new avenues for simulating complex quantum many-body systems within accessible optical architectures.

item.title: 2026 World Quantum Cannes Festival makes its debut
item.description: You haven’t missed it yet—on Nov. 17-18, 2026, the quantum community will gather in Cannes, France to be immersed in all aspects of quantum technologies, network, and enjoy the beautiful location where absolutely everything is an artform.

item.title: Barium titanate's optical properties emerge more clearly after decades of widely varying measurements
item.description: A KAIST-led research team has characterized how light propagates through and is absorbed by barium titanate (BTO), a promising material for next-generation optical communication devices. By clarifying optical properties that had been difficult to determine because of the material's complex internal structure, the study provides a foundation for designing these devices.

item.title: Upgraded microscope can now watch individual quantum particles in motion
item.description: Energy can be carried in a number of ways: by electrons, the particles that underpin all modern electronics, as well as by quasiparticles, the results of different particles interacting with one another at the quantum level. Columbia chemist Milan Delor has been watching these different forms of energy flow with an instrument called stroboSCAT, a unique microscope that uses strobe-like light pulses to capture particles and quasiparticles as they move through different materials.

item.title: New perovskite system extends room-temperature spin polarization via successive quantum wells
item.description: A research team led by Lu Haipeng, a professor in the Department of Chemistry at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), has achieved a breakthrough in preserving spin information for optoelectronic technologies. The team has developed a perovskite chiral multiple quantum-well system that maintains spin polarization approximately 300 times longer at room temperature. The study opens new possibilities for future quantum technologies and next-generation spin-based applications.

item.title: Atomic defects leave telltale optical fingerprints in quantum material
item.description: The tiny atomic defects so important for future quantum technologies can be difficult to spot. Fortunately, they leave behind some clues. The defects can alter how a material responds to light, producing a distinctive optical fingerprint that scientists can measure. The challenge is figuring out which fingerprints belong to which defects.

item.title: High-pressure setup unlocks detailed measurements of organized structures in turbulent flows
item.description: Turbulent flows are ubiquitous: they are found in clouds, in the ocean and even on other planets. Yet despite their chaotic nature, they also form large-scale structures that can be calculated and predicted. For example, while long streaks of clouds may appear orderly from the outside, their interiors are characterized by intense turbulence.

item.title: Quantum interference keeps two atoms bound despite enough energy to break apart
item.description: How can something remain intact when it should naturally break apart? This question has been addressed by researchers at RPTU. Their work has led to the experimental observation of an unusual quantum state in which two atoms remain bound together even though they possess enough energy to separate. The results have been published in the journal Nature Physics.

item.title: Optical experiment demonstrates the strong Mpemba effect in a single qubit
item.description: Typically, after a physical system is disturbed, it can gradually return toward a state of thermal equilibrium by exchanging heat with its surroundings. Thermal equilibrium is a state in which there is no net transfer of heat between the system and its surroundings.
